mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which triggers a sell-off in equities, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 35% of instances when both HOUST and INDPRO decline from prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a slowdown in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the 12-month moving average signals an impending economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 35% of instances during late-cycle expansions when HOUST falls below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle during a tight labor market, which reduces corporate profitability and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls from prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 35% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain disruption (indicated by a decline in industrial production below its 6-month moving average), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 30% of instances when INDPRO falls below its 6-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.
